subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a first-class AI-safety taxonomy that permits external plugins to emit operator-facing safety events through a host-owned, manifest-authorized capability?
rationale: The taxonomy, authorization model, emitter provenance, and public plugin contract are new security-sensitive product surfaces; automation cannot decide whether this permanent trust boundary belongs in OpenClaw.

options.title: Sponsor host-owned capability
options.body: Adopt the taxonomy after redesigning it around validated manifest policy, runtime-created emitters, host-stamped identity, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

options.title: Keep safety diagnostics internal
options.body: Do not expose external plugin emission and limit any taxonomy to core or explicitly trusted bundled-plugin producers.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Defer this PR and its dependent exporter and UI work until a narrower operator need and ownership model are approved.

recommendation.title: Sponsor host-owned capability
recommendation.body: Adopt the taxonomy after redesigning it around validated manifest policy, runtime-created emitters, host-stamped identity, documentation, and installed-plugin proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this person to plugin contract policy and security-sensitive manifest boundaries.
